description: Eight leaky integrators wired into each other through a random mixing matrix, with clippers and DC blockers in the loop: a self-oscillating instrument from steady tones to chaos

params.text: Sets how much that node's signal is fed into the matrix, 0 to 1
Sets how much of each integrator leaks away: thin and fast-decaying at the bottom of its travel, close to pure integration and heavy at the top
Multiplies everything going through the matrix, from once to a thousand times over, and it is the control that carries the module from silence through tones into saturated chaos
Attenuates the signal at the in jack before it is injected into the nodes, 0% to 100%
Re-rolls the random mixing matrix, which is a different instrument every time

inputs.text: Added to that node's gain knob, a fifth of its travel per volt
A signal injected into all eight nodes, with the sign alternating from node to node
A rising edge through 1V re-rolls the random mixing matrix

outputs.text: The left side of the eight nodes spread across the stereo field at equal power
The right side of the eight nodes spread across the stereo field at equal power
All eight nodes on one eight-channel cable, ±5V each

notes: this plays itself. With nothing patched, a tiny internal noise floor keeps the network from settling at zero, so it makes sound as soon as it is in the rack.
the matrix seed is saved with the patch, so a saved patch reopens sounding as it did.
the two lamps follow the level of the left and right outputs.

inputs.0:
±5V · continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
inputs.9:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
